meta_title: PhishLens: see why an email is phishing
meta_desc: Free, open-source Chrome extension that checks emails in Gmail and Outlook for phishing and shows why: the wording, the links, the sender's authentication and the attachments.
og_desc: Open-source Chrome extension for Gmail and Outlook: a verdict above every email, one score per check, and the words and signals behind it.
og_alt: PhishLens: see why an email is phishing. Gmail and Outlook.
footer_text: PhishLens. Free and open source, GNU AGPL-3.0 license. No cookies on this site.
hero_tag: Chrome extension · Gmail + Outlook · 8 languages · open source
hero_h1: See why an email is phishing.
hero_lead: PhishLens adds a verdict above every email in Gmail and Outlook: one score per check, the signals it found, and the words that weighed most. Click Scan, or let it check new mail on its own.
shot_alt: Two PhishLens banners above emails in Gmail. The first says the email looks like phishing, with scores for wording 97%, links 88% and sender 74%, chips for a Safe Browsing hit, a DMARC failure and a Spamhaus listing, and the words that drove the verdict. The second says the email looks safe because the sender is on the trusted list.
shot_caption: The banner PhishLens adds above an email (drawing of the real interface; try the same analysis below).
r_langs: languages checked on real phishing (the text model reads 22)
r_caught: phishing caught by the whole system, in recent emails nobody had looked at
r_latency: median scan of a typical email on a CPU-only server
r_false: of legitimate emails flagged as phishing (1 of 414)
results_note_html: Measured on PhishLens Cloud on October 24, 2026 with the public benchmark: 1,812 of 2,000 recent phishing emails in several languages, drawn from those nobody looked at while tuning (95% confidence interval 89.2% to 91.8%), and 1 of 414 legitimate emails (297 from public mailing lists, 117 from real inboxes; 0.0% to 1.4%). The scan time is the median for a typical email (about 250 tokens); a short one takes about 65 ms. An order of magnitude, not a guarantee: see how it was measured and the known limitations.
live_note: Read from the server when the page loads. Counters reset when the server restarts.
checks_intro: Real bank and university emails use the same words as phishing, so a text model on its own flags them. PhishLens checks the evidence before it decides.
chk_wording: A multilingual model (mmBERT-small, distilled from a larger phishing detector) scores the text in 22 languages; LIME shows the words that pushed the verdict.
chk_links: Every real link target, including the one behind "Click here", checked against Safe Browsing, PhishTank, URLhaus and Spamhaus.
chk_sender: SPF, DKIM and DMARC show who really sent it. Forwarded mail does not borrow the forwarder's trust.
chk_att: PDFs (scanned ones through OCR), QR codes, Office macros and remote templates, ZIP, RAR and 7z archives and calendar invites.
chk_inbox: Conversations, image-only mail and links to files shared on Drive, OneDrive or Dropbox.
popup_alt: The PhishLens popup after scanning an email: a phishing verdict, one score per check, threat-intelligence badges and the words behind the decision.
popup_caption: The popup, for files and pasted text.
att_alt: Attachment results under an email: a scanned PDF invoice with a QR code flagged as phishing, a Word document with macros flagged as phishing, and a PDF marked safe.
att_caption: Attachment results, shown under the email's attachments.
f_explain: A score per check, the signals found, and the words that pushed the text model, so you can judge for yourself.
f_mail: A Scan button next to the subject in Gmail and Outlook on the web; files and pasted text in the popup.
f_auto: Optional: new mail is checked as it arrives, marked Safe or Phishing? in the list, with a notification.
f_private: No account. Emails are analysed in memory and not stored; your history stays in your browser. Run your own server and no email leaves your computer.
f_acc: Mark each verdict right or wrong and see how PhishLens performs on your real mail, with a CSV export.
f_open: Licensed under the GNU AGPL-3.0, with a threat model, CodeQL and more than 300 automated tests run on every change.
how_read: The text, the real link targets, the sender and, in Gmail, the full original headers.
how_score: A multilingual model for the wording, a model and rules for the links, rules for the sender and where the links lead.
how_verify: Authentication results and four threat-intelligence sources, before any verdict.
how_explain: A verdict, a score per check, the signals found and the words behind it, above the email.
try_intro: This box uses the same server as the extension. Nothing is stored, but please use test emails, not private ones.

install_intro: PhishLens is not on the Chrome Web Store yet: load it by hand, it takes about two minutes.
install_s1_html: Download PhishLens-extension-….zip from the latest release and unzip it.
install_s2_html: Open chrome://extensions and turn on Developer mode (top right).
install_s3_html: Click Load unpacked and select the unzipped folder.
install_s4_html: Open an email in Gmail or Outlook on the web and click Scan with PhishLens next to the subject.
backend_own_html: Your own, private: run it with Docker, then pick Local in the extension settings.
install_more_html: Python without Docker, configuration and deployment: see the quickstart.
